title: A Wall Card Stops Being Text — It Becomes a Diagram | vitalii.no
description:
A wall-mounted study kiosk used to print the same flat text card for every subject — my own son's first verdict was 'I see no change.'

Problem: The kiosk's answer zone showed one string per card: a big question, a big answer, a rule underneath. Every subject looked identical, so a child staring at the wall learned nothing about what a compound word or a one-step equation actually looks like.

How it works: The card component was rebuilt in React and TypeScript to draw through roughly 30 templates spread across six diagram compositions — focus, break down, transform, context, map, compare. Nothing new had to be generated: math templates read straight off the existing question data, cloze pulls from the reading text, compounds come from the word list, and every unknown or missing template still falls back to the old plain card so a stale build never shows garbage.

Result: The kiosk went from printing the same flat card for every subject to a diagram built from the actual answer data — verified live with a framed card, a composition badge, and a grammar rule rendering correctly in the footer.
